findings: Base UI 1.8.0 exposes the public parts, controlled callbacks, event details, rendering hooks, positioning controls, and React support needed for Foundry's selected complex-control families.
Foundry must keep public state, validation, topology, refs, localization, styling, recovery, queueing, announcements, and package declarations behind private adapters.
Base UI Menu and Tabs intentionally keep disabled collection items focusable; the approved Foundry public contract was aligned to that accessible discovery behavior.
Base UI Toast parts are usable, but Foundry requires a private queue, timer, announcer, and multi-viewport focus coordinator to preserve its public contract.
Native field and action controls do not require Base UI and remain fully Foundry-owned.
The functional catalog exists, but its public state, styling, accessibility, package, and verification rules are inconsistent across control families.
Complex controls duplicate focus, dismissal, collection, and positioning responsibilities that mature headless libraries already maintain.
The default skin has implicit and consumer-wide CSS effects and does not provide complete recipes for the overlay and navigation family.
The repository does not yet expose a release package or one canonical product gate set.

The current skin imports through React JavaScript, renders a provider wrapper, declares values at :root, and selects generic tags, roles, descendants, and raw literals; each conflicts with the approved isolation direction.
Current controls expose only partial control and state hooks and do not provide a complete owned-part surface for fields, feedback, overlays, navigation, or portaled content.
A DOM-free provider requires resolved skin identity on each recipe-bearing owned element; that same-element identity also makes nested providers and portals independent of DOM ancestry.

Mature token systems and Base UI's unstyled state surface support generated semantic tokens plus one Foundry-owned recipe layer; W3C criteria require rendered focus, contrast, forced-color, zoom, and non-color evidence rather than token-table inspection alone.

findings.summary: Append-only document allocation conflicts with promoting a non-top modal's owned floating child directly after that modal.
findings.minimum_correction: Define one deterministic behavior for an owned floating child opened from a non-top modal, including refusal or insertion, hiding, close, and recovery.

reviews.conclusion: Token sources, validation, forced colors, serialization, and much of the runtime boundary are exact, but recipe expressiveness, rendered font sizing, and non-top-modal child layering still require implementation-time invention.
